report_name: ShinyHunters Leaks 1.6M RingCentral Records After Vishing Attack

threat_actors.name: ShinyHunters
threat_actors.description: A notorious extortion group that claimed responsibility for the RingCentral data breach. They gained initial access via a vishing attack, stole 1.6 million customer records, and leaked the data after a ransom was not paid.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through data theft and public leaks (double-extortion model).

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Voice
attack_patterns.description: The attacker conducted a voice phishing (vishing) call to a RingCentral employee, impersonating a trusted entity to manipulate the employee into divulging their password for initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: ShinyHunters used the employee password stolen via vishing to gain access to internal RingCentral systems containing customer data.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor exfiltrated over 623GB of customer data, likely using web services to make the traffic appear legitimate.

identities.name: RingCentral
identities.description: A major provider of cloud communication services that suffered a data breach where 1.6 million customer account records were stolen by ShinyHunters via a vishing attack.

identities.name: Have I Been Pwned
identities.description: A security organization and database that verified the RingCentral breach and added the leaked data to its service.

infrastructure.name: ShinyHunters Data Leak Site
infrastructure.description: The dark web site where ShinyHunters listed RingCentral, issued a ransom demand, and later published the 623GB archive of stolen customer data.

indicators.name: Anomalous Customer Data Access by Non-Technical Accounts
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Customer Data Access by Non-Technical Accounts
id: 2b1c8d7e-9a0f-4b3c-8e7f-6a5b4c3d2e1f
status: experimental
description: Detects when user accounts associated with non-technical departments (e.g., sales, marketing) perform large-scale data queries or exports from customer databases, which could indicate a compromised account being used for data collection as seen in the RingCentral breach.
references:
  - https://thenextweb.com/news/shinyhunters-ringcentral-leak-voice-phishing-ey
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-16
tags:
  - attack.t1078
  - attack.collection
level: medium
logsource:
  category: database
  product: generic
detection:
  selection:
    user_department:
      - 'sales'
      - 'marketing'
      - 'human resources'
    query_row_count|gt: 10000
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects when user accounts associated with non-technical departments (e.g., sales, marketing) perform large-scale data queries or exports from customer databases, which could indicate a compromised account being used for data collection.

indicators.name: Anomalous Large Data Egress to Residential ISP
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Large Data Egress to Residential ISP
id: 8f7e6d5c-4b3a-4c2d-8e1f-0a9b8c7d6e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects large volumes of data being transferred from a corporate network to IP addresses associated with residential ISPs, which could indicate data exfiltration through a compromised employee's home network.
references:
  - https://thenextweb.com/news/shinyhunters-ringcentral-leak-voice-phishing-ey
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-16
tags:
  - attack.t1567
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    dst_ip_category: 'residential'
    bytes_out|gt: 500000000 # 500MB
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects large volumes of data being transferred from a corporate network to IP addresses associated with residential ISPs, which could indicate data exfiltration through a compromised employee's home network.

indicators.name: Suspicious Help Desk Request for Password Reset
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Help Desk Request for Password Reset
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects urgent and unsolicited help desk requests for password resets or MFA token sharing, especially those originating from external phone numbers, which may indicate a social engineering attempt like vishing.
references:
  - https://thenextweb.com/news/shinyhunters-ringcentral-leak-voice-phishing-ey
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-16
tags:
  - attack.t1566.004
  - attack.initial_access
level: high
logsource:
  product: generic
  service: helpdesk
detection:
  selection:
    keywords:
      - 'urgent password reset'
      - 'share MFA token'
      - 'need password now'
    source: 'external_phone'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects urgent and unsolicited help desk requests for password resets or MFA token sharing, especially those originating from external phone numbers, which may indicate a social engineering attempt.
